method: Curated momentum and quality setups drawn from this run's insider, congressional, analyst and price-action work. p is the Jul 17 close from stockanalysis.com. buy is ~4% below the close at support; stop is set by type (core -11%, value -10%, momentum -12%, speculative -18% from the buy); sell is a ~18% objective from the buy (~30% for speculative). stockanalysis.com's fundamentals API returned 404 this run, so analyst price targets were not available and percentage rules were used throughout — noted for transparency.

ideas.why: Record 3-2-1 crack spreads and up 3.1% on a day the S&P fell 1%.
bull: Nymex 3-2-1 crack hit a record $64.58/bbl on Jul 8
Refining margins have nearly tripled in 2026
Up more than 80% YTD and still making highs
bear: A Hormuz de-escalation compresses the whole trade
ideas.thesis: The Gulf war made refined products scarce, not crude. Valero converts that scarcity into cash faster than any producer, and reverse-DCF puts its implied growth at just 8.9% — the lowest in the book.

ideas.why: Largest US refiner; +2.2% Friday, +80% YTD on the same crack-spread engine.
bull: MPLX midstream cash flow underpins the dividend
$5.7B TTM FCF against a $312 share price
bear: Margin cycle can roll over in a quarter
ideas.thesis: Same trade as Valero with more leverage — both operating and financial. Implied growth 9.1%.

ideas.why: Sumitomo Mitsui bought $318.7M of stock at $53.96 on Jul 15, lifting its stake +222%.
bull: SMFG now holds 8,566,379 shares and gets a board seat
Largest single insider print of the week across the whole market
bear: Purchase price adjusts over a two-month reference period
Smaller and more volatile than GS or JPM
ideas.thesis: When a strategic partner buys a fifth of a billion dollars of stock in the open market and takes a board seat, that is a different signal from a director buying $20,000.

ideas.why: CEO bought ~$1.0M and a director bought $366K — both on Jul 17, same day.
bull: CEO Gail Boudreaux added 2,725 sh at $367.79, +2% to her stake
Director Ramiro Peru bought 1,000 sh at $366.05 the same day
$201.1B TTM revenue against a ~$80B market cap
bear: Managed care has been broken all year on medical cost trend
Insurer accounting — excluded from the reverse-DCF
ideas.thesis: Same-day buying by the CEO and a board member in a sector everyone has given up on is the classic setup. It is also the classic value trap, so size it small.

ideas.why: Rose ~1% while the S&P fell 1% — Brent $88.10 and a Hormuz blockade.
bear: $88 Brent already prices a lot of war premium
ideas.thesis: The most liquid way to own the geopolitical bid. Implied growth 15.5% flatters a commodity business at a cyclical high.

ideas.why: Traffic-led comps and best-in-class unit economics — rare in restaurants right now.
bull: New-unit returns among the best in the group
Comps driven by traffic, not price
ideas.thesis: A genuine unit-growth story that has nothing to do with AI or oil — useful diversification when leadership is this narrow.

ideas.why: Flat on Friday while the semis around it fell 4.5% — relative strength worth noting.
bull: Ethernet displacing InfiniBand in AI back-ends
bear: Premium multiple in a de-rating group
ideas.thesis: If the AI trade survives in a narrower form, the network is the last piece to get cut. Implied growth 16.5% is modest for the quality.

ideas.why: Naval reactors and SMR components — revenue today, not a 2032 story.
bull: Defence budget insulation from the cycle
ideas.thesis: The nuclear theme without the pre-revenue risk. Decisive Point's $19.1M buy into Standard Nuclear on Jul 16 says capital is still flowing into the fuel cycle.

ideas.why: Gas turbines are sold out for years — the genuine bottleneck in adding generation.
bull: Turbine slots booked into the late 2020s
bear: Very high expectations embedded in the price
ideas.thesis: You cannot build a data centre without power, and you cannot build power without turbines. The constraint is physical.

ideas.why: Rep. Thomas Kean Jr bought Jun 1 at $55.26; the stock closed Jul 17 at $49.56, below his fill.
ideas.thesis: Gas is the swing fuel for data-centre load. Buying below where a disclosed congressional buyer filled is a reasonable place to start.

ideas.why: Two 10% holders each bought ~$3.77M at $12.29 on Jul 10 — an unusually clean cluster.
bull: Iconiq and director Griffith each bought 306,399 sh
ideas.thesis: The cleanest two-buyer insider cluster in the book, but it is a story stock until the P&L says otherwise.

ideas.why: Largest US nuclear fleet; the utility that trades like a growth stock.
bear: Priced for a great deal of AI demand
ideas.thesis: If AI power demand is real, this is the purest listed expression. If it is not, this is an expensive utility.
